# Judges Chapter 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_289.jpg, JDG_page_290.jpg, JDG_page_291.jpg

### Israel Fights Benjamin

#### The Assembly at Mizpah

1. All the Israelites came out and assembled together before the LORD at Mizpah — from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, including those from Gilead across the Jordan — united as one.

2. The leaders of all the people and all the tribes of Israel took their places in the assembly of God's people: 400,000 sword-bearing foot soldiers.

3. (The Benjaminites heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah.) The Israelites said, "Tell us — how did this terrible thing happen?"

4. The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered: "My concubine and I went to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.

5. "During the night, the men of Gibeah came after me. They surrounded the house, intending to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.

6. "So I took my concubine, cut her body into pieces, and sent them throughout the land of Israel, because these men committed a vile and outrageous act in Israel.

7. "All of you are Israelites. What is your verdict? What should be done?"

8. All the people stood up together and said, "Not one of us will go home. Not one of us will return to his house.

9. "Here is what we'll do to Gibeah — we'll go up against it by lot.

10. "We'll take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to get supplies for the army so they can deal with Gibeah of Benjamin as it deserves for this outrage in Israel."

11. So all the men of Israel gathered against the city, united as one.

12. The tribes of Israel sent messengers throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What is this terrible thing that has happened among you?

13. "Hand over those worthless men in Gibeah so we can put them to death and purge the evil from Israel." But the Benjaminites refused to listen to their fellow Israelites.

#### The First Two Battles

14. Instead, the Benjaminites rallied from their towns to Gibeah to fight the Israelites.

15. That day the Benjaminites mobilized 26,000 swordsmen from their towns, plus 700 elite soldiers from Gibeah itself.

16. Among these troops were 700 elite left-handed warriors, each of whom could sling a stone at a hair without missing.

17. Israel, not counting Benjamin, mobilized 400,000 swordsmen — all experienced fighters.

18. The Israelites went up to Bethel and asked God, "Which tribe should lead the attack against Benjamin?" The LORD answered, "Judah goes first."

19. So the Israelites set out the next morning and camped near Gibeah.

20. The men of Israel marched out to fight Benjamin and took up battle positions at Gibeah.

21. But the Benjaminites charged out of Gibeah and cut down 22,000 Israelites that day.

22. The Israelite army regrouped and formed their battle lines again in the same place as before.

23. The Israelites went up and wept before the LORD until evening. They asked the LORD, "Should we go fight our brothers the Benjaminites again?" The LORD answered, "Go up against them."

24. So the Israelites advanced against Benjamin a second day.

25. And Benjamin came out from Gibeah to meet them again, cutting down another 18,000 Israelites — all of them experienced swordsmen.

#### Victory on the Third Day

26. Then all the Israelites — the entire army — went up to Bethel. There they sat and wept before the LORD, fasting all day until evening, and they presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to the LORD.

27. The Israelites inquired of the LORD (the ark of God's covenant was there in those days,

28. and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, was serving before it). They asked, "Should we go out once more against our brothers the Benjaminites, or should we stop?" The LORD answered, "Go up. Tomorrow I will hand them over to you."

29. So Israel set up ambushes around Gibeah.

30. On the third day, the Israelites went up against Benjamin and took positions against Gibeah as before.

31. The Benjaminites came out to meet them and were lured away from the city. As before, they began killing Israelites — about thirty — along the roads leading to Bethel and Gibeah, and in the open fields.

32. The Benjaminites said, "We're defeating them again, just like before!" But the Israelites had planned, "We'll retreat and draw them away from the city onto the roads."

33. The main Israelite force moved from its position and regrouped at Baal-tamar, while the Israelite ambush burst out from its position west of Geba.

34. Ten thousand of Israel's finest warriors launched a frontal assault on Gibeah. The battle was intense. The Benjaminites did not realize that disaster was about to strike.

35. The LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel. That day the Israelites killed 25,100 Benjaminite swordsmen.

36. The Benjaminites saw that they were beaten. The Israelites had given ground to Benjamin because they trusted the ambush they had set near Gibeah.

37. Then the men in ambush charged into Gibeah, spread out, and put the entire city to the sword.

38. The prearranged signal between the main force and the ambush was a great cloud of smoke rising from the city.

39. When the Israelites retreated in battle, Benjamin had begun killing about thirty Israelites and thought, "We're winning — just like the first battle!"

40. But then the column of smoke began rising from the city. When the Benjaminites looked back, they saw the whole city going up in flames.

41. Then the Israelite soldiers turned to attack, and the Benjaminites panicked. They realized disaster had overtaken them.

42. They fled before the Israelites toward the wilderness, but the battle caught up with them. Meanwhile, Israelites coming from the towns were killing them from every side.

43. They surrounded the Benjaminites, pursued them, and trampled them down near Gibeah on the east.

44. Eighteen thousand Benjaminites fell — all of them brave warriors.

45. The rest turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites picked off 5,000 of them along the roads. They kept pursuing as far as Gidom, killing 2,000 more.

46. The total number of Benjaminites who fell that day was 25,000 — all of them brave, experienced swordsmen.

47. But 600 men escaped to the wilderness and reached the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed for four months.

48. The Israelites then went back through the Benjaminite towns, putting everyone to the sword — people, animals, everything they found. They burned every town they came to.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Civil war as theological collapse:** This is the darkest chapter in Judges. Israel — the people called to conquer Canaan — now turns on itself. The question "Who shall go up first?" (v.18) is the same question asked in 1:1, but now the "enemy" is a brother tribe. The book has come full circle — from external conquest to internal annihilation.

**God's mysterious delays (vv.21-28):** Israel loses 40,000 men before God grants them victory. Why? The text doesn't say directly, but it shows that Israel approached the first two battles with self-confidence, not with fasting and offerings. Only after the third inquiry — with fasting, burnt offerings, and peace offerings — does God say "I will give them into your hand." The progression from casual confidence to broken desperation mirrors the book's theology: Israel cannot win through sheer numbers or moral superiority. Even a just cause requires dependence on God.

**The destruction of Benjamin (v.48):** Israel uses cherem — the language of holy war reserved for Canaanite cities — against its own people. "Men to beast to all that was found" echoes the destruction of Jericho. Benjamin has become Canaan in the eyes of Israel. The horror is complete.

— PNEUMA, AI Translator
